entries.subject: terraform-lb-idle-timeout

scriptRef.notMeasurableLocally: An Application Load Balancer is an AWS service and cannot run on localhost; no cloud account is used.

entries.notes: Terraform AWS provider documentation for aws_lb, read 2026-11-12: "`idle_timeout` - (Optional) Time in seconds that the connection is allowed to be idle. Only valid for Load Balancers of type `application`. Default: 60." The provider source (internal/service/elbv2/load_balancer.go, main branch, read 2026-11-12) has a schema Default for it: "idle_timeout": { Type: schema.TypeInt, Optional: true, Default: 60, DiffSuppressFunc: suppressIfLBTypeNot(awstypes.LoadBalancerTypeEnumApplication) }, so Terraform sets and reconciles 60 when the attribute is absent, for application load balancers only (the DiffSuppressFunc). The same documentation page gives the type: "`load_balancer_type` - (Optional) Type of load balancer to create. Possible values are `application`, `gateway`, or `network`. The default value is `application`." tripcurve uses the default only when the type is application or absent (absent means the documented application). The value follows from the file itself and may support PASS or FAIL.

entries.subject: terraform-sqs-visibility

scriptRef.notMeasurableLocally: An SQS queue is an AWS service and cannot run on localhost; no cloud account is used.

entries.notes: Terraform AWS provider documentation for aws_sqs_queue, read 2026-11-12: "`visibility_timeout_seconds` - (Optional) Visibility timeout for the queue. An integer from 0 to 43200 (12 hours). The default for this attribute is 30." The provider source (internal/service/sqs/queue.go, main branch, read 2026-11-12) has a schema Default for it: "visibility_timeout_seconds": { Type: schema.TypeInt, Optional: true, Default: defaultQueueVisibilityTimeout, ValidateFunc: validation.IntBetween(0, 43_200) }, so Terraform sets and reconciles 30 when the attribute is absent. The SQS developer guide says: "The default visibility timeout for a queue is 30 seconds". The value follows from the file itself and may support PASS or FAIL.

entries.subject: terraform-lambda-timeout

scriptRef.notMeasurableLocally: A Lambda function is an AWS service and cannot run on localhost; no cloud account is used.

entries.notes: Terraform AWS provider documentation for aws_lambda_function, read 2026-11-12: "`timeout` - (Optional) Amount of time your Lambda Function has to run in seconds. Defaults to 3. Valid between 1 and 900." The provider source (internal/service/lambda/function.go, main branch, read 2026-11-12) has a schema Default for it: names.AttrTimeout: { Type: schema.TypeInt, Optional: true, Default: 3, ValidateFunc: validation.IntBetween(1, 900) }, so Terraform sets and reconciles 3 when the attribute is absent. The Lambda developer guide agrees: "The default value for this setting is 3 seconds, but you can adjust this in increments of 1 second up to a maximum value of 900 seconds (15 minutes)." The value follows from the file itself and may support PASS or FAIL.

entries.subject: lambda-sqs-batching-window
entries.citationName: Lambda event source mapping batching window

scriptRef.notMeasurableLocally: A Lambda event source mapping is an AWS service and cannot run on localhost; no cloud account is used.

entries.notes: AWS Lambda API reference, read 2026-11-12: "For Kinesis, DynamoDB, and Amazon SQS event sources, the default batching window is 0 seconds." The Terraform provider has NO schema default for it (internal/service/lambda/event_source_mapping.go, main branch, read 2026-11-12: "maximum_batching_window_in_seconds": { Type: schema.TypeInt, Optional: true }, sent only `if v, ok := d.GetOk(...)`), so when the attribute is absent Terraform does not send or manage it; AWS applies its own default at create and later changes outside Terraform are not corrected. Its absence from the files therefore does not establish 0: the value is used only as an ASSUMED value, and a result that rests on it is unresolved.
